input.prompt: Freeflow on Codex only delivers its session-start guidance. Can you write a Freeflow driver for Codex that does what Codex's hooks allow, like the mod does on Claude Code?

required: schema v1: each kind's required fields, its values, and no field it does not name
redaction replaces keys and tokens in a command before it is written
events append sets seq per log under a lock, redacts and cuts commands, and refuses what is not schema v1
two writers of one log never share a seq; a stale lock is cleared, a live one makes the batch fail
the event log stays out of the store's Git, and a home with only a log still takes a store
checkpoint and release commit the session's event summary since it took the task
summarize counts dropped lines and leaves out what came before since
a second session's take is refused with the holder and its last sync, and allowed after a release; each hold is pushed
a session holds one task at a time: take refuses a second, switch releases the first
the menu lists the open tasks of the project whose tasks name the folder's remote, or of every project elsewhere (P95), and says what this session holds
removing a task or a project is a pushed commit that Git history keeps, and task numbers are not reused
a task with no project: created where no project names the folder, listed in the menu, moved into a project and out again without reusing its number
outside a Freeflow store, every project and task command says a store is needed
the session is read from the environment: Claude Code's IDs, a cloud session's link, or Freeflow's own variables
task here --scan remembers where a task's repository is on this machine, so recovery resolves its pointers (P96)
task here --rules adds the store's rules and the folder's and held task's project rules after the menu, and nothing without it
a resumed session takes back the task its end released (F36), never one released on purpose or taken since
task release --ended --no-push commits the ended hold here only, and the next sync pushes it (SPEC-012 P3)
checkpoint refuses a store task this session does not hold, naming task take (F36)
every recorded input follows Codex's generated schema for its event
hooks.json names the driver for every event it answers, with fork, the bundle unlimited and SessionEnd within 3 s
each output is the shape Codex's output schema documents, and events that steer nothing print nothing
session start: the guidance, then the task menu; after Codex compacts, the guidance again and the task's bundle after Codex's summary
a model request past 50, 60 or 70 percent or the notice point: its row or notice reaches the model at the next tool call or prompt, once a cycle
a checkpoint after the notice, through Track Work's script, makes the bundle after Codex's next compaction current; checkpoint --compact is refused, naming Codex's thresholds
the event log: a scripted Codex session's lines are schema v1, in order, kept until the turn ends and written in one run, never contents
each conformance test names a yes claim of the driver, and every yes claim has one (SPEC-006 4.7)
capabilities.mjs lists Codex's claims from the file the driver writes
with Freeflow off for the session's folder, only the claims are written, every one no, and nothing else runs
with the event log off, the menu and rows still come and no line is kept
without a store: the guidance and what is missing, the event log still kept, no rows
token_usage missing: no row and no notice, and one freeflow line a session says so
the window and the notice point come from Codex's config: model_context_window and the auto-compact limit
a tool call's paths: a file tool's fields and apply_patch's files, never the patch's text
every handler fails open: no session, a home it cannot write, or an unknown event exits 0 with the guidance at most
the driver waits for input the host writes after starting it
live host manifests share one package identity and the canonical skill kernel
Agent Plugins 1.0 manifest rejects component path fields
Agent Plugins 1.0 manifest rejects invalid plugin names and schemas
OpenCode uses the canonical skill source without a second tree
Gemini SessionStart uses the optional matcher-free lifecycle configuration
Gemini's hook must resolve its adapter under Gemini and under Claude Code
Codex's hooks run the driver on every event it answers, fork included and the bundle uncut (SPEC-012)
Hermes uses the portable Agent Plugins package rather than a native Python plugin
